region_name: Northeast & East: Deer Park, Gray Wolf, Royal Basin, Dungeness, Dosewallips, Lake Constance
summary: The dry rain-shadow corner of Olympic National Park and the adjoining Buckhorn Wilderness: Deer Park's high car-camp and the waterless Grand Ridge, the deep Gray Wolf and Cameron valleys with their high passes, the quota-limited jewel of Royal Basin under Mount Deception, the Upper Dungeness and Marmot Pass approaches, and the long Dosewallips valley (reached only by a 6.5-mile road walk since a 2002 washout) leading to Hayden Pass, Anderson Pass and the notoriously steep Lake Constance. Bear canisters are required in every park camp; Royal Basin, Lake Constance and Grand Ridge's Roaring Winds are quota areas.

nodes.name: Deer Park Trailhead (Deer Park Campground & Ranger Station)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Frontcountry campground, first-come first-served, self-register; $15/night; tents only; open June to mid-October depending on road and snow (NPS camping page, 2026). Backpackers leaving from here still need a wilderness permit.
camp.water: No potable water at Deer Park - bring all water.
camp.notes: Fire pits with grates, picnic tables, accessible pit toilets, animal-proof food storage; firewood gathering prohibited; in wind watch for branches falling from trees killed in a 1988 fire. Ranger station staffed intermittently in summer and fall.

nodes.description: The gravel road gives up at the very top of the world, where a handful of tent sites perch among wind-bent firs and sun-silvered snags. Below, the lowlands and the blue Strait spread out like a map, and to the south the jagged Needles bite the sky.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a weathered wooden ranger cabin and a brown trail sign on a post; midground: silvery dead snags from the old burn and dark subalpine firs, a tent on a gravel pad; sky: dithered light blue fading to white near the horizon; landmark: grey sawtooth peaks (the Needles) far to the south, a strip of blue sea to the north. EGA: light grey, dark green, brown, light blue, white.

nodes.name: Obstruction Point Trailhead
nodes.description: The road ends on a bare gravel shoulder of the mountains, higher than most birds bother to fly. Every direction is ridge and snow and sky, and the wind never quite stops talking.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: gravel parking pad with a single wooden sign and a low rock wall; midground: rolling tan-and-green alpine tundra with a snowbank; sky: deep blue at top dithered to light cyan; landmark: white Mount Olympus far to the southwest above dark ridges. EGA: brown, light grey, white, blue, light cyan.

nodes.name: Slab Camp Trailhead (USFS, Slab Camp Trail #838 / Deer Ridge Trail)
nodes.description: A gravel turnaround at the end of a long potholed forest road, where two paths slip away into the trees. One climbs a rhododendron ridge toward Deer Park; the other drops through quiet forest to the Gray Wolf River.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a rough gravel lot with a dusty car and a brown Forest Service sign; midground: second-growth firs and pink rhododendron blossoms; sky: pale blue patches through branches; landmark: a forked trail post pointing two ways. EGA: brown, dark green, light magenta, light blue.

nodes.name: Gray Wolf Trailhead (USFS, Lower Gray Wolf Trail #834)
nodes.description: A tiny pullout in a hairpin bend of the forest road, with room for three cars and the sound of the Gray Wolf River somewhere below. The trail dives straight downhill into moss and alder.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a hairpin curve of gravel road with one parked car; midground: mossy maples and a steep path dropping away; sky: barely visible, green-grey canopy; landmark: a glint of white water far below. EGA: dark green, light green, brown, grey.

nodes.name: Upper Dungeness Trailhead (USFS)
nodes.description: A big gravel lot sits just across a bridge over the milky Dungeness River, ringed by enormous Douglas-firs. A vault toilet, a picnic table, and a kiosk crowded with notices mark the gateway to Royal Basin and the Buckhorn Wilderness.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a brown Forest Service kiosk with a map and a picnic table; midground: wooden road bridge over a grey-green river, cars parked under huge fir trunks; sky: narrow blue slot between trees; landmark: the trail mouth disappearing into old-growth. EGA: brown, dark green, cyan-grey water, light blue.

nodes.name: Upper Big Quilcene Trailhead (USFS)
nodes.description: At the end of a winding forest road the Big Quilcene River chatters past a small parking area. Giant cedars and hemlocks crowd the start of the trail that climbs to Marmot Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: gravel parking with a privy and a trail sign reading MARMOT PASS; midground: huge red-brown cedar trunks and ferns; sky: dark green canopy with a few blue chinks; landmark: a white-water creek at the edge of the lot. EGA: brown, dark green, light green, white, grey.

nodes.name: Tubal Cain Trailhead (USFS)
nodes.description: A plain gravel lot at the end of the forest road, with a kiosk and a shelter just inside the trees. Old mining stories and a lost airplane wait up the valley.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: gravel lot and a wilderness registration kiosk; midground: a log footbridge over Silver Creek and rhododendrons; sky: light blue between firs; landmark: a rusty ore cart silhouette on the trail sign. EGA: brown, dark green, light magenta, grey.

nodes.name: Dosewallips Road End (current Dosewallips trailhead, below the road washouts)
nodes.description: The paved road simply stops at a barrier, and the old road beyond belongs to walkers, bicycles and the river now. Cars line the shoulder; somewhere ahead the Dosewallips has chewed the road away.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: an orange-and-white road barrier and cars parked on a gravel shoulder; midground: an empty asphalt road curving into tall firs, grass in the cracks; sky: light blue with puffy white clouds; landmark: a roaring grey-green river at the road edge. EGA: light grey road, dark green, brown, white water, light red barrier.

nodes.name: Brinnon
nodes.description: A small Hood Canal community strung along the highway between the water and the hills, where the Dosewallips River meets salt water. It is the last stop before the long road walk into the Dose valley.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a two-lane highway with a mailbox and a roadside sign; midground: a small general store with a porch (fictional), tidal flats; sky: soft grey-blue over Hood Canal; landmark: forested foothills rising behind. EGA: grey, brown, cyan water, dark green.

nodes.name: Quilcene
nodes.description: A quiet logging-and-oyster town at the head of Quilcene Bay, home to the Forest Service office for the Buckhorn Wilderness trails. Trucks and hikers both pass through on Highway 101.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: highway with a Forest Service sign and a pickup truck; midground: small wooden storefronts (fictional names) and stacks of oyster shells; sky: pale blue with high clouds; landmark: green ridges of the eastern Olympics. EGA: brown, grey, dark green, light blue.

nodes.name: Sequim
nodes.description: A sunny town in the rain shadow of the Olympics, where lavender fields grow under drier skies than almost anywhere else in western Washington. It is the jumping-off point for the Dungeness and Gray Wolf trailheads.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a lavender field in purple rows; midground: a farm road and a few houses; sky: bright blue, nearly cloudless (rain shadow); landmark: the snowy wall of the Olympics to the south. EGA: light magenta, dark green, white, bright blue.

nodes.name: Roaring Winds Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA camp (Grand and Badger Valleys quota area, which includes Deer Park to Obstruction Point). Recreation.gov Oct 2026 data: 1 party / 6 people per night; max group 6.
camp.water: NO water at all - carry every drop in.
camp.notes: Single very exposed ridge site; NPS warns several bear canisters have been lost by rolling down the mountainside from here - wedge yours. Cathole only. Trail to it is steep, exposed and loose in places.

nodes.description: A single tent pad clings to the spine of Grand Ridge, and the wind lives here full time. On a clear evening the whole interior of the Olympics glows orange at once, and there is not one drop of water in sight.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: one small tent with guy lines straining, a bear canister wedged between rocks; midground: steep grey-brown scree falling away on both sides; sky: dithered orange-to-violet sunset with streaks of cloud; landmark: white Mount Olympus floating above blue ridges to the southwest. EGA: brown, grey, light red, magenta, white, blue.

nodes.name: Grand Ridge / Elk Mountain Primitive Trail junction (Grand Ridge high point)
nodes.description: The trail tops out on the shoulder of Elk Mountain at the highest point of any maintained trail in the park's northeast. Below, Grand Valley's lakes shine like dropped coins, and marmots whistle from sunny rocks.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a weathered junction sign and a cairn; midground: tundra with tiny pink and white flowers and a whistling marmot on a boulder; sky: intense blue with a few white puffs; landmark: Moose and Grand lakes glinting in a green valley, Mount Olympus beyond. EGA: brown, light green, white, blue, light cyan.

nodes.name: Deer Ridge Trail junction (Three Forks Trail)
nodes.description: Just below the campground the path splits: one way plunges toward Three Forks, the other wanders down Deer Ridge toward Slab Camp. A bench of meadow and stonecrop sits at the fork.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a two-armed wooden signpost; midground: rock garden with yellow stonecrop and blue phlox; sky: light blue; landmark: the deep forested Gray Wolf valley falling away. EGA: brown, yellow, light blue, dark green.

nodes.name: Gray Wolf River bridge (Slab Camp Trail / Upper Gray Wolf Trail junction)
nodes.description: A sturdy bridge spans the Gray Wolf in a hush of old trees, with Camp Tony's flats nearby. Downstream the lower trail is broken by a washout; upstream the path wanders toward the park.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a plank bridge with log railings; midground: clear green river over cobbles, mossy boulders; sky: thin blue strip over the canyon; landmark: tall cedars leaning over the water. EGA: brown, cyan, dark green, light green.

nodes.name: Slide Camp (Gray Wolf River, Olympic National Forest)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic National Forest (Buckhorn Wilderness) - no Olympic NP permit needed here; wilderness rules apply (max 12 people).
camp.notes: Reported as small and uneven (2017 Mountaineers report). Location and elevation estimated from trip reports: about 2.3 mi above the Slab Camp bridge, roughly 600 ft higher. Canisters still strongly advised.

nodes.description: A cramped little camp squeezed between the river and an old slide of rock and roots. It is a fine place to stop when the light is going and the park boundary is still ahead.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a lumpy tent site on roots; midground: a jumble of boulders from an old slide and the river beyond; sky: dim green-grey canopy; landmark: a fallen giant log bridging the slope. EGA: brown, dark grey, dark green, cyan.

nodes.name: Lower Gray Wolf Trail end (washed-out former bridge site)
nodes.description: The lower trail ends abruptly where a flood tore out the bridge; a stub of the old span clings to the far bank. Across the water, unreachable, the path from Slab Camp continues.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: the trail ending at a raw cutbank; midground: a broken bridge abutment and boulder-choked river; sky: grey-green through alders; landmark: a lone timber of the old bridge on the far side. EGA: brown, grey, white water, dark green.

nodes.name: Olympic National Park boundary (Upper Gray Wolf Trail)
nodes.description: A small brown sign on a fir trunk announces the national park. From here on, every night needs a permit and every snack rides in a bear can.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a brown NPS boundary sign nailed to a tree; midground: trail winding along a forested bench; sky: green canopy; landmark: arrowhead emblem on the sign. EGA: brown, dark green, light green.

nodes.name: Gray Wolf River Trail / Cameron Creek Trail junction (Three Forks)
nodes.description: Three valleys come together here, and their rivers argue loudly about which way is downhill. Signs point to Deer Park, Cameron Pass and Gray Wolf Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a three-way trail sign; midground: a log footbridge over rushing water; sky: dark canopy with shafts of light; landmark: three forested valleys meeting. EGA: brown, dark green, white water, light cyan.

nodes.name: Three Forks Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.water: Grand Creek, Cameron Creek and the Gray Wolf River.
camp.notes: Forested sites near Grand Creek; toilet available; fires allowed only in existing rings with dead-and-down wood (below 3,500 ft). OpenStreetMap marks a trail shelter here (status unverified).

nodes.description: Deep in the bottom of the valley, three rivers meet under cedars and firs. The campsites are soft with needles, the water is loud enough to sing you to sleep, and Deer Park is a long, steep 3,400 feet above.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tent under big trees and a small fire ring; midground: an old log shelter and a footbridge over a creek; sky: only green-black canopy with a few stars; landmark: the confluence of white-water streams. EGA: dark green, brown, white, cyan, black.

nodes.name: Gray Wolf Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.notes: Forested sites near the river; a 2025 WTA trip report mentions a new privy and a spacious site. Fires only in existing rings (below 3,500 ft).

nodes.description: A roomy camp in tall forest beside the Gray Wolf, where the river is bright and cold. It is the last easy evening before the valley begins to climb in earnest.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent and bear canister by a mossy log; midground: the green-white river through firs; sky: dappled light; landmark: a new wooden privy roof peeking from the trees. EGA: dark green, brown, cyan, white.

nodes.name: Camp Ellis

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 6.
camp.water: Gray Wolf River and side streams.
camp.notes: Small camp; fires only in existing rings (below 3,500 ft). Toilet: use toilet if available, otherwise cathole.

nodes.description: A small, quiet camp tucked against the river as the Gray Wolf valley narrows. Moss drips from every branch and the trail beyond starts to tilt upward.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a single tent on a flat; midground: mossy boulders and a narrowing canyon; sky: grey-green canopy; landmark: a frothy cascade. EGA: dark green, light green, white, grey.

nodes.name: Falls Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.water: Gray Wolf River and the creek below Cedar Lake.
camp.notes: Camp sits in and below a meadow at about 3,900 ft; the Cedar Lake way trail starts at the top of the meadow near the campsites. NPS camp listing still says fires in existing rings, but NPS also bans fires above 3,500 ft - treat as no fires.

nodes.description: The forest opens into a meadow loud with falling water. Above, the Gray Wolf comes down in white ribbons, and a faint path slips off toward a hidden lake.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tents at the edge of a green meadow; midground: a waterfall pouring over dark rock; sky: light blue with a wisp of cloud; landmark: a steep forested headwall. EGA: light green, white, grey, dark green, light blue.

nodes.name: Cedar Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Camp listed on Recreation.gov ('Cedar Lake (No Campfires)') but hidden from online booking - arrange with the Wilderness Information Center (360-565-3100).
camp.notes: Remote, little-visited subalpine lake reached by a 2.1 mi primitive way trail from Falls Camp.

nodes.description: A shy, still lake hides above marshy meadows and a maze of fallen trees. Few people come here; the loudest thing is a jay complaining about you.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: soggy meadow with tufts of grass and a fallen log; midground: a dark blue lake ringed with subalpine fir; sky: soft blue with a high cloud; landmark: rocky peaks of the upper Gray Wolf reflected in the water. EGA: blue, dark green, light green, grey, white.

nodes.name: Gray Wolf Pass
nodes.description: A notch of shattered rock and late snow between the Gray Wolf and the Dosewallips. From the top, Mount Deception and the Needles crowd the eastern sky, and the trail drops in long switchbacks toward Dose meadows.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a rocky saddle with a snow patch and a wooden post; midground: talus slopes with tiny flowers; sky: deep blue with a few clouds; landmark: jagged grey peaks (Mount Deception) to the east. EGA: grey, white, blue, brown, light magenta.

nodes.name: Gray Wolf Trail junction (Main Fork Dosewallips Trail)
nodes.description: Here the Main Fork trail breaks out of the forest into meadows of waist-high cow parsnip, and the Gray Wolf trail climbs away to the north. Mount Mystery and Mount Deception loom behind.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a junction sign half-hidden in tall white-flowered plants; midground: wet green meadow; sky: light blue; landmark: craggy peaks with snowfields above the valley. EGA: light green, white, brown, grey, blue.

nodes.name: Lower Cameron Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 6.
camp.notes: Forested sites near Cameron Creek. Recreation.gov listing says fires allowed in existing rings, but the camp sits above 3,500 ft where NPS prohibits fires - treat as no fires. Trail here seldom maintained; heavy brush.

nodes.description: A small forest camp beside Cameron Creek, out of the wind and out of the way. The creek is clear and cold, and the trail in both directions hides under brush.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent by a mossy creek; midground: thick brush and alder; sky: patches of blue through firs; landmark: a log footbridge half-awash. EGA: dark green, light green, cyan, brown.

nodes.name: Grand Pass Trail / Cameron Pass Trail junction (upper Cameron Creek)
nodes.description: Three trails meet where Cameron Creek's valley bends. One leaps straight up the wall toward Grand Pass, one pushes up-valley into Cameron Basin, and one follows the creek down toward Three Forks.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a weathered three-way sign; midground: brushy meadow laced with little streams; sky: blue with clouds catching on peaks; landmark: an impossibly steep slope rising toward Grand Pass. EGA: light green, brown, blue, white, grey.

nodes.name: Grand Pass
nodes.description: A windy notch high above Grand Valley's lakes, where the trail tips over and plunges 2,300 feet into Cameron Creek. On one side the world is tidy lakes; on the other it is wild and steep.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a rocky saddle with a cairn; midground: steep loose scree dropping away; sky: bright blue; landmark: Grand Valley lakes glittering on one side, rugged Cameron peaks on the other. EGA: grey, brown, blue, white, light green.

nodes.name: Upper Cameron Camp (Cameron Basin)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.notes: Subalpine camp in Upper Cameron Basin; no campfires; toilet if available else cathole.

nodes.description: Cameron Basin is a bowl of meadow and snowmelt streams beneath ragged peaks and the small Cameron glaciers. Evenings here are hushed, gold, and full of marmot whistles.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent in a flower meadow with a meandering stream; midground: talus fans and snow patches; sky: dithered gold evening light; landmark: Mount Cameron's grey crags with small white glaciers. EGA: light green, yellow, white, grey, blue.

nodes.name: Cameron Pass
nodes.description: A steep gap at the head of Cameron Basin, often guarded by a lingering snow tongue. Over the top, the route drops into a hidden basin before rising again to Lost Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a snow cornice edge and loose rock; midground: a steep snowfield with boot steps; sky: deep blue; landmark: jagged ridges of Mount Cameron and Lost Peak. EGA: white, grey, blue, brown.

nodes.name: Lost Pass
nodes.description: A flowery saddle with trees blocking much of the view, perched above the headwaters of the Dosewallips. Below it the trail falls almost straight down to Dose Meadows.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a meadow of lupine and paintbrush; midground: a few clumpy subalpine firs; sky: light blue; landmark: green Dose Meadows far below. EGA: light magenta, light red, light green, dark green, blue.

nodes.name: Dose Meadows Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.water: Upper Dosewallips River (a bridge crosses its source just above camp).
camp.notes: No campfires; pit toilet may be available. WTA notes it is buggier than Bear Camp and has no shelter. Strategic junction for Lost Pass, Cameron Pass and Hayden Pass.

nodes.description: The young Dosewallips meanders through a wide meadow at the foot of the high passes. Evenings bring deer, mosquitoes and a sky that stays light long after the sun drops behind Hayden Pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tents on a meadow bench, a small stream; midground: a log bridge over the infant river; sky: pale gold to blue gradient; landmark: steep green slopes rising to Hayden Pass. EGA: light green, yellow, blue, brown, white.

nodes.name: Hayden Pass
nodes.description: From this high gap, Mount Olympus and the Bailey Range fill the west and Mount Anderson rises to the south. A snow cornice may cling to the east rim into midsummer.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a narrow trail cresting a saddle with a lingering snow lip; midground: meadow slopes falling to the Elwha side; sky: vast blue; landmark: white Mount Olympus and the Bailey Range on the horizon. EGA: white, light green, blue, grey.

nodes.name: Dosewallips Road washout and bypass trail (January 2002)
nodes.description: In 2002 the river took a bite out of the road, and it has never been put back. A narrow bypass path scrambles up and around the gap before dropping back onto quiet, empty pavement.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: broken asphalt ending in a ragged edge; midground: a raw cutbank and a skinny dirt path climbing around it; sky: light blue over firs; landmark: the white-water Dosewallips churning below. EGA: grey, brown, white, cyan, dark green.

nodes.name: Lake Constance Route junction (old Lake Constance trailhead on the closed Dosewallips Road)
nodes.description: An unremarkable bend in the abandoned road, except for a small sign and a path that goes nearly straight up. Somewhere 3,200 feet above is one of the most beautiful lakes in the Olympics.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a cracked old road and a tiny brown sign; midground: blackened burned snags on a steep slope; sky: light blue; landmark: the steep wall of Mount Constance's foot. EGA: grey, black, brown, light blue, dark green.

nodes.name: Half Acre Rock
nodes.description: A boulder the size of a house sits in the dim canyon of Constance Creek, dwarfing the trees around it. A pair of campsites hide in its shadow - the only soft ground on the whole route.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a giant grey boulder with moss on top; midground: dark old-growth trunks and a white creek; sky: barely visible through canopy; landmark: the tiny figure of a hiker for scale. EGA: grey, dark green, white, black.

nodes.name: Lake Constance

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA area. Recreation.gov Oct 2026 data: 6 parties / 20 people per night (max group 6) plus one group site (7-12 people, 12 people max).
camp.notes: Designated sites only, on the far (north) shore reached by the path along the east edge; composting toilet in the rock field is operational (NPS 6/5/26) while the south vault toilet is closed; do not urinate in the composting toilet. Stock prohibited.

nodes.description: Deep, turquoise and cold, the lake fills a cirque under the great walls of Mount Constance like a jewel set in granite. Sunken logs lie like bones in the shallows near the outlet.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: sunken silver logs in clear shallows; midground: turquoise lake with a rocky shore and a few tents; sky: bright blue; landmark: the towering grey cliffs and snowfields of Mount Constance. EGA: cyan, light cyan, grey, white, dark green.

nodes.name: Dosewallips Ranger Station & Dosewallips Campground (old road-end trailhead)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Former drive-in campground, now walk/bike-in only. Recreation.gov has a hidden 'Dose Campground' division (call the WIC); a 2024 trip-report comment says no permit is needed - unverified, ask the WIC.
camp.notes: Picnic tables removed but fire rings remain (June 2025 report); privies and bear lockers reported; a new bike rack near the old ranger station (June 2025). Bikes allowed on the road to here, not on trails beyond. Ranger station is historic/derelict, not a staffed office.

nodes.description: At the end of the long road walk the old campground waits, half returned to the forest. A shuttered ranger cabin, empty fire rings and a bike rack mark where the real trail finally begins.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: an empty fire ring and a bicycle leaning on a rack; midground: a small shingled ranger cabin with boarded windows; sky: green canopy and a slice of blue; landmark: Dosewallips Falls white through the trees. EGA: brown, grey, dark green, white, light blue.

nodes.name: Dose Forks Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.notes: Fires allowed in existing rings with dead-and-down wood; pit toilet may be available. About 8 mi from the current road-end parking (1.4 mi past the old ranger station).

nodes.description: Where the Dosewallips splits in two, a forest camp sits on the tongue of land between the forks. Both rivers are loud, green and full of snowmelt, and trails lead up each valley.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tent and fire ring under big firs; midground: two rivers meeting in white foam; sky: green-gold light; landmark: a junction sign with arrows to Hayden Pass and Anderson Pass. EGA: dark green, brown, white, cyan, yellow.

nodes.name: Constance Pass Trail junction (Main Fork Dosewallips)
nodes.description: A signpost points uphill to Constance Pass on a trail that wastes no time climbing. Below, the Main Fork trail keeps traversing high above the roaring river.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a signpost with two arms; midground: steep forest slope with a switchback; sky: patches of blue; landmark: the river glinting far below. EGA: brown, dark green, cyan.

nodes.name: Burdick Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Listed on Recreation.gov as 'Burdick Creek' but hidden from online booking - contact the WIC.
camp.notes: WTA: a single site for one small tent right beside the trail, with a bear wire (wires no longer allowed for food storage - canisters required). Coordinates and elevation estimated from WTA mileage along the NPS trail line.

nodes.description: A single cramped tent spot squeezed beside the trail at a splashing side creek. It is a place for the tired, not the picky.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tiny tent pitched beside the trail tread; midground: a mossy creek tumbling over rocks; sky: deep forest green; landmark: an old bear-wire cable between two trees. EGA: dark green, grey, white, brown.

nodes.name: Deception Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12. Separate stock camp nearby.
camp.water: Deception Creek - silty with glacial flour from Mystery Basin; clogs filters (settle or pre-filter).
camp.notes: Largest camp area on the Main Fork, nearly halfway to Hayden Pass; fires allowed in existing rings; pit toilet may be available.

nodes.description: The biggest camp on the Main Fork spreads under tall trees beside a creek the color of skim milk. The water carries ground-up rock from glaciers high on Mount Mystery.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: several tents and a fire ring; midground: a milky grey-blue creek over boulders; sky: canopy with sun shafts; landmark: a glimpse of icy Mount Mystery up the side valley. EGA: dark green, light grey, cyan, brown, white.

nodes.name: Bear Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12. Separate stock camp.
camp.notes: No campfires; shares a privy. WTA describes a shelter at the meadow edge among fireweed and breathtaking views.

nodes.description: A lonely camp in the upper meadows with an old trail shelter standing knee-deep in pink fireweed. Mount Mystery and Mount Deception tower behind like a stage set.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a log shelter with a shake roof surrounded by magenta fireweed; midground: green meadow with a tent; sky: light blue with drifting clouds; landmark: jagged Mount Deception and Mount Mystery. EGA: brown, light magenta, light green, grey, blue.

nodes.name: Sunnybrook Meadows Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 6.
camp.water: Streams near the meadow; NO water on the trail below until about 0.5 mi below the meadows.
camp.notes: No campfires; cathole only. NPS: above the meadows the trail tread is poor and failing in some rock-slide sections.

nodes.description: After a brutal dry climb, the trail tumbles into sunny meadows threaded by little streams. Marmots, lupine and long views of the Dosewallips valley make the effort worth it.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a sparkling streamlet through flowers; midground: tilted green meadow with one tent; sky: bright blue; landmark: rocky ridges of Mount Constance's backside. EGA: light green, blue, light magenta, grey, white.

nodes.name: Constance Pass
nodes.description: A high, airy saddle between the Dosewallips and the Dungeness, with Home Lake glittering just below. The rock here is red and green, and the wind smells of snow.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a rocky saddle with a few twisted whitebark-like pines; midground: Home Lake below in a green bowl; sky: deep blue; landmark: the rugged backside of Mount Constance and Warrior Peak. EGA: brown, light red, dark green, blue, white.

nodes.name: Home Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 6.
camp.notes: No campfires; cathole only; camp in pre-existing impacted sites. About 10 mi from the Upper Dungeness Trailhead or 13.6 mi from the Dosewallips road end.

nodes.description: A small round lake sits in a meadow cup just below Constance Pass, still as a mirror in the morning. Snow often lingers on the slopes above well into summer.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: grassy lakeshore with a single tent; midground: calm blue lake with reflections; sky: soft morning blue; landmark: snow-streaked peaks above the lake. EGA: light green, blue, white, grey.

nodes.name: Boulder Shelter (USFS camp)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic National Forest, Buckhorn Wilderness - no NPS permit needed; max group 12; no fires above 3,500 ft.
camp.water: Creek at Boulder Shelter - the most reliable water on the Upper Dungeness trail.
camp.notes: Flat campsites; the old shelter was standing in 2014 but avalanche-snapped trees litter the area and the shelter may not survive (WTA). Junction: Constance Pass Trail to Home Lake (3.6 mi) and Upper Dungeness Trail to Marmot Pass (1.7 mi). Canisters strongly advised.

nodes.description: An old shelter crouches among boulders and avalanche-snapped trees at the head of the Dungeness valley. Trails fan out from here toward Marmot Pass and Home Lake.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tired log shelter with a mossy roof among boulders; midground: snapped tree trunks pointing every which way; sky: light blue; landmark: steep avalanche chutes on the slopes. EGA: brown, grey, dark green, white, light blue.

nodes.name: Camp Handy (USFS camp and shelter)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic National Forest, Buckhorn Wilderness - no NPS permit needed; max group 12.
camp.notes: Cedar-shingle shelter beside an open riverside meadow; popular; gray jays and chipmunks raid careless campers (WTA). Fires permitted below 3,500 ft per Buckhorn Wilderness rules (verify any seasonal burn bans).

nodes.description: A cedar-shingle shelter sits at the edge of a broad riverside meadow, with a view up the valley toward Constance Pass. Gray jays watch every sandwich with great interest.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a three-sided cedar shelter with a picnic of bread on a log and a gray jay on a branch; midground: grassy meadow along the river; sky: light blue; landmark: distant peaks up valley. EGA: brown, light green, grey, cyan, light blue.

nodes.name: Royal Basin Trail junction (Upper Dungeness Trail, Royal Creek footlog)
nodes.description: About a mile up the Dungeness, a footlog spans Royal Creek and a signpost turns hikers uphill toward Royal Basin. The other branch keeps strolling up the river toward Camp Handy.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a squared footlog bridge over a rushing creek; midground: a wooden sign pointing right to ROYAL BASIN; sky: green canopy; landmark: giant Douglas-firs. EGA: brown, dark green, white, cyan.

nodes.name: Marmot Pass
nodes.description: A broad, grassy pass where three trails meet and the whole eastern Olympics line up for inspection. Marmots whistle from the rocks and whitebark pines twist in the wind.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a meadow saddle with a three-way sign and a marmot on a rock; midground: contorted white-barked pines; sky: brilliant blue; landmark: Warrior Peak and Mount Constance across the Dungeness valley. EGA: light green, white, grey, blue, brown.

nodes.name: Camp Mystery (USFS)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic National Forest, Buckhorn Wilderness - no NPS permit needed; max group 12.
camp.water: Good water source reported (2017 trip report).
camp.notes: Popular camp under the last trees below Marmot Pass, less than half an hour from the pass; fires prohibited (above 3,500 ft).

nodes.description: The last trees before the meadows shelter a busy camp with a dependable stream. In the morning the light pours over the ridge onto the tents like warm honey.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: several tents among subalpine firs; midground: a small stream through heather; sky: dawn gold to blue; landmark: the grassy rise toward Marmot Pass. EGA: dark green, yellow, light green, blue.

nodes.name: Shelter Rock Camp (USFS, Big Quilcene)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic National Forest, Buckhorn Wilderness - no NPS permit needed; max group 12.
camp.notes: Riverside flat where the trail leaves the river to climb; the namesake shelter is long gone. Elevation: WTA ~3,600 ft, SummitPost ~3,650 ft, USGS DEM at the OSM camp point ~3,820 ft. Fires: at or near the 3,500-ft line - assume no fires.

nodes.description: A flat in the old-growth beside the Big Quilcene marks the end of the easy walking. The shelter that named it vanished long ago; only the river remembers.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a flat campsite with a rock fire ring; midground: huge hemlocks and a white-water river; sky: green canopy; landmark: a moss-covered boulder. EGA: dark green, brown, white, grey.

nodes.name: Buckhorn Pass
nodes.description: The Tubal Cain trail crosses this high shoulder on its way around Buckhorn Mountain, with ridge-top views east to Puget Sound country and west to the Dungeness peaks.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: rocky trail on a ridge with lupine; midground: steep meadow slopes; sky: blue; landmark: Buckhorn Mountain's summit block. EGA: brown, light magenta, light green, blue, grey.

nodes.name: Buckhorn Lake junction (Tubal Cain Trail)
nodes.description: A signed fork where a narrow side path drops to tiny Buckhorn Lake and the main trail climbs toward the ridge.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a small brown sign; midground: open hillside of trillium and lupine; sky: light blue; landmark: a glimpse of a small lake below. EGA: light green, white, blue, brown.

nodes.name: Buckhorn Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic National Forest, Buckhorn Wilderness - no NPS permit needed.
camp.water: Plenty of water near the lake (WTA).
camp.notes: A few campsites along a narrow, up-and-down side trail; huckleberries in some camps.

nodes.description: A tiny lake tucked under Buckhorn Mountain, ringed with huckleberry bushes. In late summer the berries stain fingers purple.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: huckleberry bushes with purple berries; midground: a small round lake; sky: light blue; landmark: Buckhorn Mountain's rocky slopes. EGA: dark green, magenta, blue, grey.

nodes.name: Big Timber Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12. Designated stock camp here.
camp.notes: Fires in existing rings (below 3,500 ft); pit toilet. About 10.7 mi from the current road end.

nodes.description: True to its name, this camp hides among enormous old trees along the West Fork. The forest floor is soft, dim and quiet, and the river whispers instead of roars.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tent dwarfed by a giant fir trunk; midground: ferns and mossy logs; sky: almost none, deep green; landmark: a column of light falling on the river. EGA: dark green, brown, light green, yellow.

nodes.name: Diamond Meadows Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12. Designated stock camp here.
camp.notes: Fires in existing rings; pit toilet. The footbridge just above Diamond Meadow is out - the river must be forded (twice) before Honeymoon Meadows.

nodes.description: A forest camp by a pretty bend of the West Fork, where the valley briefly opens. Just upstream, the old bridge is gone and the river must be waded.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: tents by a gravel bar; midground: the river with the broken stubs of an old bridge; sky: light blue opening in the canopy; landmark: forested walls of the valley. EGA: dark green, grey, cyan, brown, light blue.

nodes.name: Honeymoon Meadows Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.notes: No campfires; pit toilet. The unbridged West Fork ford between Diamond and Honeymoon Meadows can be hazardous in spring and after heavy rain.

nodes.description: Open meadows and young firs fill the upper West Fork valley below Mount Anderson's ice. Deer browse at dusk, and the river glows silver in the long evening.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: grassy meadow with a tent and a deer; midground: a braided silver river; sky: dusky blue with first stars; landmark: snowy Mount Anderson massif at the head of the valley. EGA: light green, white, blue, grey, brown.

nodes.name: LaCrosse Pass Junction Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov division 'LaCrosse Junction (No Campfires)' is hidden from online booking - contact the WIC. NPS lists 'Lacrosse Pass Junction' among West Fork campsites.
camp.notes: Junction of the LaCrosse Pass Trail (6.4 mi to the Duckabush River Trail) with the West Fork trail.

nodes.description: A small camp at the fork where the LaCrosse Pass trail heads off south through steep meadows. Camp Siberia is only a few steps beyond.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a junction sign with LACROSSE PASS arrow; midground: tents in young firs; sky: light blue; landmark: steep green slopes rising south. EGA: brown, dark green, light green, blue.

nodes.name: Camp Siberia

camp.reservation_or_quota: Olympic NP wilderness permit required (Recreation.gov, reserved in advance; no trailhead self-registration). Not a quota camp: as of Oct 2026 Recreation.gov showed no nightly cap (shown as 100) for this camp area. Max group 12.
camp.water: West Fork Dosewallips River and side streams.
camp.notes: No campfires; pit toilet. Last camp below Anderson Pass (about 1 mi); very little water at the pass itself.

nodes.description: A chilly little camp in a shady pocket below Anderson Pass, where cold air pools at night - hence the name. It is the last good water before the pass.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a frosty tent and a steaming mug; midground: dark firs and a cold stream; sky: pale dawn blue; landmark: the notch of Anderson Pass above. EGA: white, dark green, light cyan, grey.

nodes.name: Anderson Pass
nodes.description: A low forested pass that links the Dosewallips and the Quinault, a revolving door for long traverses. A short steep path from here climbs the moraine toward what remains of Anderson Glacier.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a trail sign with arrows to Enchanted Valley and Dose Forks; midground: subalpine firs and heather; sky: blue; landmark: the grey moraine and Mount Anderson's crags above. EGA: brown, dark green, grey, blue, white.

nodes.name: Anderson Glacier overlook (end of Anderson Moraine Trail)
nodes.description: The moraine path ends on a rubble crest above a bowl of grey rock, meltwater and a shrinking remnant of ice beneath Mount Anderson. The glacier that once filled it has mostly gone, and the silence is enormous.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a rocky moraine crest with a cairn; midground: a grey basin with a milky meltwater pond and dirty snow; sky: blue with high cloud; landmark: dark crags of Mount Anderson with small white ice patches. EGA: grey, light grey, white, light cyan, blue.

nodes.name: LaCrosse Pass
nodes.description: A steep climb from the West Fork tops out on a meadowed crest, looking south into the Duckabush country. Wildflowers and wind share the summit.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a narrow pass with a sign; midground: meadow slopes plunging on both sides; sky: blue with cumulus; landmark: Duckabush valley and distant peaks to the south. EGA: light green, brown, blue, white.

nodes.name: Royal Creek Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA area (Royal Basin/Royal Lake). Recreation.gov Oct 2026 data: 3 parties / 30 people per night; max group 12. Online reservations limited to a shorter summer season; outside it, call the WIC.
camp.notes: Forested sites near Royal Creek, about 4 mi from the trailhead; cathole only (composting toilets are at Royal Lake only). Trail closed to stock at the park boundary. Fires (fact check 2026-10-08): NO campfires. NPS's Royal Basin page (updated 2026-01-28) says 'No campfires in Royal Basin' and lists Royal Creek as one of the basin's three camp areas; the camp also sits near 3,700 ft, above the park's 3,500-ft fire limit. Recreation.gov's 'Royal Creek' division text still says campfires are permitted in established rings; that conflicts with NPS, and the stricter NPS rule is used here.

nodes.description: Halfway up the valley, a few forest sites listen to Royal Creek racing down from the basin. It is a gentler first night for those who start late.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tent under firs beside a bouncing creek; midground: talus fans from the valley walls; sky: blue strip above; landmark: a white waterfall ribbon streaming down a far cliff. EGA: dark green, grey, white, cyan, blue.

nodes.name: Lower Royal Meadow Camp

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA area. Recreation.gov Oct 2026 data: 2 parties / 12 people per night; max group 6.
camp.notes: Subalpine sites about 1 mi below Royal Lake; nearest toilet at Royal Lake; no campfires.

nodes.description: The valley opens into a sloping meadow beside Royal Creek, with the first big views of the peaks ahead. Wildflowers crowd the trail in July.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a tent in a flowery meadow; midground: Royal Creek meandering; sky: bright blue; landmark: craggy peaks (The Needles) rising ahead. EGA: light green, light magenta, cyan, grey, blue.

nodes.name: Royal Lake

camp.reservation_or_quota: QUOTA area (Royal Basin/Royal Lake). Recreation.gov Oct 2026 data: 8 parties / 30 people per night, max group 6; plus 1 group site (7-12 people). Camping limited year-round; online reservations for a shorter summer season, early reservations recommended for May 1 - Sept 30; outside the online season call the WIC.
camp.notes: Designated sites only (NPS camp map shows about 9 individual sites plus a group site - count from map image). Composting toilet at the north end - use it for all solid waste and toilet paper. Seasonal ranger station (summer only) east of the lake. Trees unsuitable for hanging; canisters required 24 hours a day. Rodents actively try to get into food here (NPS, 6/5/26). Camping is at Royal Lake, NOT in the Upper Basin, unless arranged with the WIC.

nodes.description: Royal Lake sits in a cradle of meadow and talus under a crown of the highest peaks in the eastern Olympics. A seasonal ranger's tent hides up valley, and a hidden waterfall sings behind it.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a small tent beside the lake with a bear canister; midground: clear green-blue lake rimmed with subalpine fir and rock; sky: dithered pink-to-blue dusk; landmark: Mount Deception and The Needles, grey and jagged, streaked with snow. EGA: cyan, dark green, grey, white, light magenta, blue.

nodes.name: Upper Royal Basin (tarns, about 5,700 ft)

camp.reservation_or_quota: Recreation.gov division 'Upper Royal Basin (No Campfires)' is hidden from online booking - contact the WIC (360-565-3100); Oct 2026 data showed 3 parties / 12 people, max group 6.
camp.notes: Barren, moon-like upper basin of talus, glacial tarns and remnant snowfields; no fires; cathole only on durable surfaces. Passes Shelter Rock (a big overhanging pillow-lava boulder) and Arrowhead Meadow on the way up. Off-trail parties continue south over a ridge into Deception Basin or east into Milk Creek Basin (WTA).

nodes.description: Above the lake the trees give up and the basin turns to stone and water: milky blue tarns, polished rock and patches of old snow under Mount Deception's walls. It feels like the top of the world, and like no one has been here before you.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: a milky-turquoise tarn edged with snow and grey boulders; midground: a talus bowl with snowfields; sky: deep blue with one white cloud; landmark: the towering grey north wall of Mount Deception. EGA: light cyan, white, grey, dark grey, blue.

nodes.name: Royal Glacier (informal name; glacier remnant at the head of Royal Basin below Mount Deception)
nodes.description: At the very head of the basin, a dirty, shrinking tongue of ice clings beneath Mount Deception's cliffs. Rocks clatter down onto it in the afternoon warmth.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: grey moraine rubble; midground: a cracked, dirt-streaked ice slope with a dark crevasse line; sky: hard blue; landmark: Mount Deception's rotten-rock wall. EGA: white, light grey, dark grey, light cyan, blue.

nodes.name: Mount Deception
nodes.description: The second-highest peak in the Olympics rises above Royal Basin, all crumbling grey rock and snow couloirs. It is a climb for mountaineers, not a stroll - but from the lake it fills half the sky.
nodes.scene_art_notes: Foreground: steep snow couloir; midground: crumbling grey buttresses; sky: dark blue at zenith; landmark: the summit block with a wisp of cloud. EGA: grey, dark grey, white, blue.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Starts at the Deer Park ranger station down an old road grade to the forested Blue/Green Mountain saddle (~4,900 ft, the lowest point), then angles up the south side of Green Mountain into meadows and rounds the shoulder of Maiden Peak (~3 mi; Maiden Peak itself is a side trip, 3.5 mi one-way from Deer Park, +1,545 ft per NPS). No water on the entire Grand Ridge trail; not recommended for stock. Gain/loss scaled so Deer Park to Obstruction Point totals NPS's 2,423 ft of gain (profile shape from USGS DEM).

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: After a low saddle the trail gains about 600 ft in half a mile; tread can be hard to follow in wet or foggy weather - stay high, on the south side of the ridge. Tops out at the Grand Valley junction sign at 6,625 ft (WTA 5.25 mi from Deer Park).

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Stays high under the three summits of Elk Mountain (snow cornices persist on the ridge-top into late summer - stay on solid rock), then drops to a dip before Obstruction Point. A steep, high-angle snowfield lingers late into summer just east of the Obstruction Point parking lot and is hazardous without traction/ice axe and skills. Elk Mountain Primitive Trail branches here to Badger Valley (1.3 mi, 6,650 to 5,600 ft).
Deer Ridge Trail splits from the Three Forks Trail 0.2 mi below the trailhead (NPS brochure).

segments.snow_free_typical: lower half snow-free by about June; upper switchbacks hold snow into early summer
segments.notes: Strenuous: NPS gives 4.3 mi from Deer Park to the Gray Wolf River Trail junction with 3,416 ft of elevation loss. Hikers going down often forget they must climb all of it back out ('upside-down hike'). Expect winter conditions into early summer.

segments.snow_free_typical: lower ridge by May-June; upper meadows snow-free about late June
segments.notes: Deer Ridge Trail: 3.1 mi in Olympic National Forest plus 1.5 mi in the park (NPS brochure: total elevation loss 3,272 ft going down from Deer Park). Rhododendron tunnel in spring; grade steepens after 1.5 mi; one small trickle is the only water; Gray Wolf valley overlook and a memorial bench about 0.6 mi below the park boundary. WTA lists 4.9 mi one-way, 2,800 ft gain. Popular early-season way to reach Deer Park before its road opens.

segments.snow_free_typical: most of the year (mid-spring best for rhododendrons)
segments.notes: Lower Gray Wolf Trail #834 (USFS): 4.2 mi through dense hardwoods and conifers to the former bridge site and end of trail; grades up to 15%; stock prohibited. WTA: 8.4 mi round trip with about 1,250 ft of total gain, high point 1,500 ft; muddy; ends at a washout with part of an old bridge on the far side - do not cross. Dead end: does not connect to the park.

segments.snow_free_typical: most of the year (low elevation); icy in late fall/winter
segments.notes: Slab Camp Trail #838 follows Slab Camp Creek down to a large bridge over the Gray Wolf River (USFS says 3.1 mi; Mountaineers 2.8 mi to Camp Tony and the river; OSM 2.77 mi). The Lower Gray Wolf Trail downstream is cut by a slide about 1 mi north of this junction, so the upper Gray Wolf is reached only via Slab Camp. A Mountaineers day-hike party turned back in Nov 2024 at the bridge near Cameron Creek because the wooden bridges were iced.

Upper Gray Wolf Trail #834.2 meanders along the river past Slide Camp; generally steep in places (USFS). Mileage and ~600 ft gain from a Mountaineers route description; a 2022 report put Slide Camp about 5.2 mi from the trailhead. Over 35 downed trees counted between Slide Camp and Gray Wolf Camp in 2017; about two dozen blowdowns in 2022.

Mountaineers puts the park boundary about 6 mi from Slab Camp Trailhead; OSM measures 5.8 mi. Gain is the USGS DEM total for the bridge-to-boundary stretch (+963/-404) minus the ~600 ft before Slide Camp; loss not separable.

segments.snow_free_typical: most of the year; snow possible in winter
segments.notes: NPS: Upper Gray Wolf River Trail runs ~14.6 mi from the park boundary via Three Forks to the Main Fork Dosewallips Trail. Distance here from the NPS trail GIS line.
Short connector along the Cameron Creek Trail to Three Forks Camp and the foot of the Three Forks Trail.
Up the Gray Wolf River Trail. Distance from NPS trail GIS line.
Valley narrows and begins to climb; distance from NPS trail GIS line (consistent with WTA's 5.3 mi from Three Forks to the steep upper valley).
Steady climb up the upper Gray Wolf to the meadow and falls at Falls Camp.

Cedar Lake Way Trail (NPS 2.1 mi, 3,900 to 5,300 ft). Start is hard to find - it begins at the top of the meadow near the Falls Camp sites; after the creek crossing it is difficult to navigate through several marshy meadows and many downed trees (NPS 6/5/26).

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: WTA: 3.8 mi climb to Gray Wolf Pass; NPS high point 6,200 ft. Snow lingers in the upper basin into July.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: WTA: drops steeply over 3.3 switchbacking miles to the Main Fork Dosewallips Trail (NPS: trail ends at 3,550 ft).

Cameron Creek Trail (NPS: Three Forks to the Grand Pass Trail junction 7.0 mi, 2,150 to 4,200 ft). Two creek crossings can be difficult or impossible in heavy rain or high-country melt; the northern crossing's foot-log can be partly under water at high flow (NPS 6/5/26). Seldom maintained, heavy brush, hard to follow in places (Recreation.gov). Split point at Lower Cameron from NPS GIS line.
Remainder of the 7.0-mi Cameron Creek Trail.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Recreation.gov: the trail from Grand Pass to Cameron Creek is very steep and loose, descending about 2,300 ft in less than 2 miles. Part of NPS 'Grand Valley/Grand Pass Trail' (Obstruction Point via Grand Valley and Grand Pass to the Cameron Creek Trail, 7.7 mi). Grand Pass itself and Grand Valley belong to the neighboring Grand Valley region.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Cameron Pass Trail (NPS: 3.6 mi junction to Cameron Pass, 4,150 to 6,450 ft): typically overgrown and hard to follow below Cameron Basin; not recommended for stock. Split at Upper Cameron from NPS GIS line.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: WTA: the pass trail can be dicey when snow is present.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Cameron-Lost Pass Primitive Trail (NPS 1.9 mi): unmaintained route with steep sections and loose rock; hard to follow along creek beds and meadows. Drops into the basin below Lost Pass, then climbs to it. NPS lists the route between 6,200 and 6,450 ft, but USGS/GNIS put Lost Pass itself at 5,571 ft and the DEM agrees; gain/loss from DEM.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Lost Pass Primitive Trail (NPS 0.9 mi). Extremely steep - more than a thousand feet in under a mile; a 2017 hiker described it as 'more like a series of creeks'. Leaves the Dosewallips trail at the northeast corner of Dose Meadows. Snow into early summer.

Closed road. Mile markers in a 2021 report put the road end at about mile 8.6 and the 2002 washout roughly 10 mi from US 101; OSM routing ends about 1.1-1.3 mi below the NPS-mapped washout point. Distance approximate. Bikes allowed on the road.

Bypass trail around the washout, then abandoned paved road climbing gently up-valley past the closed USFS Elkhorn Campground (about 2.4 mi from the parking per a 2021 trip report; reported as not requiring an NPS permit) to the park boundary (old orange gate) and the Lake Constance route. NPS: Lake Constance is 5.0 mi of road from the washout area; total road walk to the old campground is 6.5 mi.
Last stretch of road to the old Dosewallips Campground and ranger station. Bikes may be ridden to the ranger station but not on trails beyond.

segments.snow_free_typical: April to November in most years
segments.notes: NPS 'Dosewallips River Trail': original trailhead (pre-washout) to Dose Forks 1.4 mi, 1,600 to 1,736 ft. Passes the Terrace Loop trail. Recreation.gov counts Dose Forks about 8 mi from the current road end.
WTA: stay right at Dose Forks, Constance Pass Trail junction at 2.5 mi from the old trailhead.
Tread high above the river; Upper Twin Creek gives a view of Calypso Falls. NPS (7/11/26): 19 trees down between the Constance Pass junction and Deception Creek, largest 3.5 ft diameter.
Open forest of silver fir with salal and a few Pacific yews (WTA). Mileage per WTA (Deception Creek at 7.8 mi from the old trailhead; Recreation.gov 14.3 mi from the current road end).
Grade steepens toward the Gray Wolf junction at 9.2 mi. NPS (7/11/26): 21 trees down between Deception Creek and Hayden Pass, largest 3 ft.

Meadows full of waist-high cow parsnip soak passing legs after rain or dew; rodent holes threaten ankles (WTA). Bear Camp at 10.9 mi from the old trailhead (Recreation.gov: 17.5 mi from the current road end).
In and out of forest and meadow with clumpy Alaska yellow-cedar. Dose Meadows at 12.6 mi from the old trailhead per WTA (Recreation.gov: 18.5 mi from the current road end).

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Cross a bridge over the river's source, then switchback into the upper basin (last water) on slopes favored by foraging black bears. The final push narrows; a winter cornice often lingers as a steep snow patch on the east rim, usually gone by August (WTA). Hayden Pass Trail continues 8.3 mi west to the Elwha (neighbor region) with an eroded, exposed section west of the pass and 2016 Hayes Fire blowdown. NOTE: NPS lists Dose Forks to Hayden Pass as 11.3 mi; WTA's 15.0 mi from the old trailhead (13.6 from Dose Forks) matches the NPS GIS trail line much better and is used here.

segments.snow_free_typical: late June or early July through September
segments.notes: Route climbs the slope just west of Constance Creek through a 2009 burn; hands needed over piles of fallen blackened trees; ribbon markers. Old growth from about 0.4 mi. Half Acre Rock at 0.8 mi with two campsites beside the creek and a brief reprieve in grade (WTA). Reliable water: the creek at the halfway point and the lake (NPS).

segments.snow_free_typical: late June or early July through September
segments.notes: Class 2 to sometimes Class 3 scramble (WTA): at about 1.3 mi the route climbs a series of ledges and small cliffs above Constance Creek using roots for holds; the top ledge has none; do not attempt when wet; descending is harder than climbing. Metal tags mark much of the way above. NPS: extremely steep, climbing 3,200 ft in 1.8 mi; requires hands; closed to stock. Route length: NPS conditions 2.0 mi, NPS route page 1.8 mi (final climb), WTA 2.2 mi. Fact check 2026-10-08: the two route legs were scaled from 0.8 + 1.2 = 2.0 mi to 0.7 + 1.1 = 1.8 mi. Both NPS (Lake Constance Route page, updated 2026-01-29: '3,200 ft climb in 1.8 miles') and Recreation.gov ('the final 1.8 miles of trail to the lake gains approximately 3,200 feet'; the lake is 6.8 mi from the new trailhead) give 1.8 mi. The Half Acre Rock split point is still an estimate. The NPS trail conditions table (6/5/26) rounds this to '2 miles, 1500' to 4700''; its 4,700 ft supports the lake elevation used here.

segments.snow_free_typical: lower part June; meadows about mid-July
segments.notes: Constance Pass Trail (NPS: 7.8 mi from the Main Fork junction to the park boundary via Home Lake, 2,182 to 5,850 ft). Relentless climb; no water until about 0.5 mi below Sunnybrook Meadows (NPS). Split distances scale the NPS GIS line to NPS's 7.8 mi total. (Recreation.gov's camp blurbs imply a shorter 2.7 mi here - conflicting.)

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Above the meadows the tread is poor and failing in some rock-slide sections (NPS). USGS DEM along the NPS trail line suggests the route crests a ridge near 6,500 ft before dropping to the pass, although NPS lists 5,850 ft as the trail's top elevation - treat the high point as uncertain.

segments.snow_free_typical: typically mid-July to early October (high country; snow can linger later on north aspects)
segments.notes: Short descent to Home Lake on the Dungeness side.

WTA: 3.6 mi from Boulder Shelter to Home Lake, crossing into the park about 1 mi above the shelter (WTA also says 2.9 mi from the boundary to the lake - small internal discrepancy). Recreation.gov: Home Lake is 10 mi from the Upper Dungeness Trailhead. Gain/loss from DEM on the NPS line plus an estimate for the USFS mile.

Switchbacks above Boulder Shelter through contorted whitebark pine, then a final northward ascending traverse to Marmot Pass where steep, somewhat exposed snowfields can linger to early July (WTA). Upper Dungeness Trail ends at Marmot Pass, 8.1 mi from the trailhead (WTA/USFS).

Steady climb without switchbacks (going up) past two good water sources, with views into the Milk Creek and Heather Creek drainages and numerous avalanche paths across the valley (WTA). A fork about 0.5 mi above Camp Handy. USFS grade 10-15%, some to 20%.

segments.snow_free_typical: about May to November (low elevation, snow/ice in winter)
segments.notes: Easy riverside walk through towering old-growth Douglas-fir; crosses the Dungeness on a stout bridge at about 2.6 mi from the trailhead. Camp Handy at 3.2 mi (USFS) or 3.4 mi (WTA).
First mile of the Upper Dungeness Trail #833.2; enters Buckhorn Wilderness at the Royal Creek footlog. Milky glacial flour tints the river.
Rolling forest walk beside the Big Quilcene among enormous cedars and hemlocks (WTA). Gain from USGS DEM along the OSM trail line.
Leaves the river; after about 3.5 mi from the trailhead the trail steepens for about three-quarters of a mile, then eases. Camp Mystery at about 4.5 mi (WTA; SummitPost 4.6 mi).

Meadow, a rise, a second meadow and the pass. Total trailhead-to-pass: USFS 5.3 mi, WTA about 5.75 mi (11.5 mi RT, 3,489 ft gain). Maximum grades 30% (USFS). Fires prohibited above 3,500 ft including Camp Mystery and Marmot Pass; don't camp on the alpine meadows at the pass.

Tubal Cain Trail #840 traverses around Buckhorn Mountain, topping out around 6,200-6,300 ft on the ridge (WTA; DEM). Buckhorn Mountain summit is about 1 mi from Marmot Pass with 900 ft gain (WTA). Distance from OSM trail line.
WTA: Marmot Pass is 2.9 mi from the Buckhorn Lake junction (OSM 2.87).
Signed side trail with steep ups and downs past a few camps to the lake (WTA); net about 130 ft lower than the junction.

Open hillside of trillium, lupine and alpine aster, then Copper Creek and the Tubal Cain mine area (camps littered with mining debris; water pouring from the mine shaft may carry unsavory substances - collect water elsewhere). Tull Canyon side trail near mile 3.0 climbs 450 ft in 0.6 mi to the 1952 B-17 crash site. Shelter and camp near the trailhead; USFS trail total 8.6 mi to Marmot Pass.

NPS West Fork: Dose Forks to Anderson Pass 9.0-9.1 mi. Split points use Recreation.gov mileages from the road end (Big Timber 10.7, Diamond Meadows 13.3, Honeymoon Meadows 15.5, Camp Siberia 16.2) and a July 2025 trip report (Big Timber just under 11).
Most creeks have footlogs or bridges (NPS).

segments.snow_free_typical: about June to October; fords high in spring melt
segments.notes: The footbridge just above Diamond Meadow is out; be prepared to ford the West Fork a couple of times before Honeymoon Meadows (NPS 6/5/26). The ford can be hazardous in spring and after heavy rain. An April 2026 party turned back at the ford beyond the meadows with snow patches and low cloud.
LaCrosse Pass Trail branches south here.
Adjacent camps.

Final climb to the pass (NPS: 4,464 ft); very little water at the pass. NPS 6/5/26: snow-free to Anderson Pass. The East Fork Quinault trail continues south from here to Enchanted Valley (neighbor region).
Anderson Moraine Trail (NPS 0.8 mi, 4,465 to 5,200 ft). Patchy snow on trail 6/5/26.

LaCrosse Pass Trail (NPS: 6.4 mi from the West Fork to the Duckabush River Trail, 3,600 to 5,566 ft; several trees down 6/5/26). Distance to the pass scaled from the NPS GIS line. The far side descends to the Duckabush (neighbor region; Lake LaCrosse is a shared node reached by other trails).
Upper Dungeness Trail; turn right just before the footlog over Royal Creek (WTA).

Switchbacks above Royal Creek; stay left at the Maynard Burn Trail junction; enter Olympic National Park (closed to stock at the boundary). Moss-carpeted fir and hemlock with a few step-over creeks (NPS: be prepared to get feet wet). Royal Creek camp about 4 mi from the trailhead (split scaled from NPS GIS to NPS's 7.2 mi total).
Talus-strewn open stretches with views up and down valley; a white-ribboned waterfall streams down a cliff about half a mile upslope; long traverses punctuated by steep switchbacking climbs (WTA).

NPS: 7.2 mi from the trailhead to Royal Lake (2,550 to 5,100 ft), moderate to steep. 2026: trail mostly snow-free to Royal Lake by late April/early May (WTA trip reports), and NPS reported snow-free to Royal Lake on 6/5/26.

Past the summer ranger station (side path to a waterfall view), under Shelter Rock's huge overhang, across a short footlog to Arrowhead Meadow, an unbridged stream, then up to the tarns at about 5,700 ft (WTA). NPS maintained Royal Basin Trail ends in the 'Shelter Rock area' (6.2 mi from the park boundary); beyond is a way trail (OSM 'Upper Royal Basin Trail', 1.05 mi). In May 2026 climbers lost the trail repeatedly in a marshy area near 5,300 ft and found continuous snow above.

segments.snow_free_typical: ice year-round; approach snow-covered into July
segments.notes: Off-trail travel on moraine and remnant ice under Mount Deception; rock is rotten and rockfall common (NPS). Distance unknown.

segments.snow_free_typical: climbing season about July to September; spring ascents need ice axe and crampons
segments.notes: Not a walk-up: NPS says the Royal Basin peaks are not walk-ups and the rock is often very rotten; be prepared for rockfall and snow hazards; in winter/spring check avalanche danger.
