hazards.name: The long Dosewallips road walk
hazards.real_world: Every Dosewallips trip starts with 6.5 mi and about 1,200 ft of abandoned road before the real trail. Hikers who plan mileage from the old trailhead arrive at camp hours late, footsore from pavement.
hazards.game_event_idea: At the barrier: (a) shoulder the pack and walk (adds a long day, +fatigue), (b) unload a bike and ride/push to the ranger station (needs 'bike' + 'bike_lock' in the car - 60% faster but the washout bypass needs a hike-a-bike: 15% chance of a scraped shin), (c) stay the first night at the USFS Elkhorn Campground on the road to split the distance, (d) turn around and pick a different trailhead.

hazards.name: Washout bypass trail
hazards.real_world: A narrow, steep path scrambles around the 2002 washout where the river ate the road.
hazards.game_event_idea: The bypass is muddy after rain: (a) go slow with trekking poles (safe), (b) hurry with a heavy pack (20% chance of a slip - lose time and morale, 5% chance of a twisted ankle), (c) carry the bike over in two trips (+time, no risk).

hazards.name: Lake Constance root ledges
hazards.real_world: A Class 2-3 scramble up ledges and small cliffs using tree roots for holds; the top ledge has none; mistakes can be fatal; descending is harder. Not to be attempted when wet.
hazards.game_event_idea: Rain begins at Half Acre Rock: (a) camp at the two sites by the rock and try tomorrow (needs extra food day), (b) climb anyway (with 'gloves' and a compact pack: 85% fine; without: 60% fine, else retreat bruised - or in Sierra mode a fall), (c) turn back to the road. Fear-of-heights companion may refuse.

hazards.name: West Fork Dosewallips fords (bridge out)
hazards.season: worst in spring melt (May-July) and after heavy rain; afternoon flows highest on warm days
hazards.real_world: The footbridge above Diamond Meadow is out; hikers ford the river a couple of times before Honeymoon Meadows. Spring or storm flows can be dangerous; an April 2026 party turned back.
hazards.game_event_idea: Standing at a cold, fast ford at 3 pm: (a) cross now unbuckled with poles (camp_shoes + poles: 90% ok; barefoot: 65%, else soaked gear and a cold night), (b) camp at Diamond Meadows and cross at dawn when melt is lower (+1 day food), (c) search upstream for a log (30% find one, costs an hour), (d) give up on Anderson Pass.

hazards.name: Cameron Creek crossings
hazards.real_world: Two crossings on the Cameron Creek Trail can be difficult or impossible in heavy rain or high-country melt; the northern foot-log can be partly under water.
hazards.game_event_idea: The foot-log is awash: (a) shuffle across with poles (70%; fail = dunked, wet sleeping bag unless in dry bag), (b) wait a day at Three Forks for the creek to drop, (c) reroute up the Gray Wolf instead.

hazards.name: Waterless, windy Grand Ridge
hazards.season: July-October; afternoon thunderstorms possible; fog anytime
hazards.real_world: There is no water anywhere on the 7.4-mi Grand Ridge trail and none at Roaring Winds camp; the ridge is exposed to wind, fog and storms; bear canisters have rolled off the mountain.
hazards.game_event_idea: At Roaring Winds: (a) you carried 4+ L per person - dinner and breakfast are fine, (b) you carried 2 L - choose: dry dinner and a thirsty morning (morale down) or hike out at dusk, (c) wind gusts: stake out the tent fully (needs 'extra_stakes') or 25% chance of a broken pole; also choose where to wedge the bear can (30% chance it rolls away if left on open ground - lose a day's food).

hazards.name: Steep snowfield near Obstruction Point
hazards.season: June into August in many years
hazards.real_world: A high-angle snowfield lingers east of the Obstruction Point lot late into summer and is hazardous without equipment and skill.
hazards.game_event_idea: Morning ice on the snowfield: (a) put on microspikes and cross (95%), (b) kick steps in trail runners (60%; fail = slide and scrape, lose time), (c) wait until noon for softer snow (+time), (d) turn back.

hazards.name: Grand Pass knee-buster
hazards.real_world: About 2,300 ft of very steep, loose trail in under 2 miles between Grand Pass and Cameron Creek.
hazards.game_event_idea: Heading down the loose scree: (a) poles and slow (safe, +30 min), (b) bound down fast (20% chance of a fall: lose time, sore knee for 2 days), (c) heavy pack over 35 lb raises fall chance.

hazards.name: Lost Pass and Cameron-Lost primitive route
hazards.real_world: Unmaintained, very steep sections with loose rock; hard to follow along creek beds and meadows; Lost Pass trail gains over 1,000 ft in under a mile; Cameron Pass dicey with snow.
hazards.game_event_idea: Fog rolls in at Cameron Pass: (a) navigate with map and compass (needs 'map_compass': 85% stay on route), (b) follow a faint boot track (55%, else lose 2 hours), (c) camp and wait out the fog (+day of food), (d) retreat to Upper Cameron.

hazards.name: Hayden Pass snow lip
hazards.real_world: A winter cornice often lingers as a stubborn steep snow patch on the eastern rim near the top of Hayden Pass.
hazards.game_event_idea: The trail vanishes under a steep snow lip: (a) chop steps with an ice axe (90%), (b) climb with microspikes (75%), (c) scramble around on loose rock (50%, else slide back down), (d) be content with the view from below.

hazards.name: Royal Basin quota and permit check
hazards.real_world: Royal Basin is a quota area: about 8 parties per night at Royal Lake, permits bulk-released and selling out; no walk-ups and no trailhead permits; deviation from the itinerary is not allowed except in emergencies; a summer ranger is stationed at the lake.
hazards.game_event_idea: During planning: (a) book on release day (success 70% for weekends, 95% midweek), (b) choose Royal Creek or Lower Royal Meadow instead, (c) day-hike only. On trail, the ranger asks for your permit: no permit = sent back down (trip ends early, gently told).

hazards.name: Bold rodents at Royal Lake
hazards.real_world: NPS reports rodents trying to get into food around Royal Lake; trees are unsuitable for hanging and canisters are required 24 hours a day.
hazards.game_event_idea: You wake to chewing sounds: (a) food is in the bear canister - the critter gives up (no loss), (b) trail mix left in the hip-belt pocket - 80% chance of a chewed pack and lost snacks, (c) shoo it away and lie awake (morale down).

hazards.name: Snow above Royal Lake
hazards.real_world: In May 2026 climbers lost the trail repeatedly in a marshy area near 5,300 ft and found continuous snow above; NPS warns of rockfall, rotten rock and snow hazards.
hazards.game_event_idea: Snow covers the way to the tarns: (a) follow the creek with a map (needs map_compass), (b) put on microspikes and climb the snow slope (with ice axe: safe; without: 30% slide), (c) enjoy the lake and skip the upper basin.

hazards.name: Rotten rock and rockfall below Mount Deception
hazards.real_world: The Royal Basin peaks are not walk-ups; the rock is often very rotten; rockfall and snow hazards are real.
hazards.game_event_idea: A rattle of stones high above: (a) retreat from the gully (safe), (b) keep scrambling toward the summit (Sierra-style danger in hard mode; in gentle mode a ranger later reminds you why peaks aren't walk-ups), (c) sit and sketch the mountain instead (journal bonus).

hazards.name: Waterless climb to Sunnybrook
hazards.real_world: The Constance Pass Trail climbs about 3,400 ft from the Main Fork with no water until about 0.5 mi below Sunnybrook Meadows; above the meadows the tread is failing in rock-slide sections.
hazards.game_event_idea: Halfway up in the heat: (a) you filled 3 L at Dose Forks - steady progress, (b) you have 1 L - ration (slower, morale down) or (c) drop back to the river and start at dawn tomorrow (+1 day).

hazards.name: Glacial silt in Deception Creek
hazards.real_world: Deception Creek drains Mystery Basin and carries glacial flour that clogs water filters.
hazards.game_event_idea: Filter slows to a trickle: (a) let a pot settle overnight (+time), (b) use chemical tablets, (c) backflush the filter (needs 'filter_backflush'), (d) force it - 40% chance the filter fails for the trip.

hazards.name: Blowdown and brush
hazards.season: worst before summer crews clear; anytime after storms
hazards.real_world: NPS reported 40 trees down on the Main Fork (7/11/26); dozens of blowdowns on the Upper Gray Wolf; Cameron trails overgrown with heavy brush.
hazards.game_event_idea: A giant fir blocks the trail: (a) climb over (10% chance of a torn rain jacket), (b) crawl under (pack snags; slower), (c) bushwhack around (map needed; time cost). Brush soaks you: rain pants keep morale.

hazards.name: Black bears in the upper Dosewallips
hazards.real_world: WTA describes slopes below Hayden Pass as beloved by foraging black bears; canisters required park-wide; a Mountaineers group saw a medium black bear near Slab Camp in Nov 2024.
hazards.game_event_idea: A bear grazes 100 yards off the trail: (a) give it space and wait (safe), (b) make noise and pass wide (safe), (c) step closer for a sketch (in gentle mode the bear wanders off and you lose 'leave no trace' points; never rewarded). At night: food in canister = no problem; food in tent = bear visit, trip ends early.

hazards.name: Upside-down hikes (Three Forks)
hazards.real_world: The Three Forks trail loses about 3,400 ft in 4.3 mi - easy going down, a grind on the way out at the end of a trip.
hazards.game_event_idea: On exit day: (a) start at dawn in the cool (safe), (b) start at noon in the heat with heavy pack (energy drain x2, 25% chance of needing a long rest and arriving after dark), (c) layover one more day to rest (needs food).

hazards.name: Potholes, slides and road work on the Dungeness roads
hazards.real_world: FR 2870/2880 are potholed; a rockslide blocked FR 2880 past Dungeness Forks (Dec 2025); NF-2870 resurfacing Oct 7-26, 2026 with flaggers and weekday closures.
hazards.game_event_idea: Driving to the trailhead: (a) take the long way via Lost Mountain Road (+15 min, safe), (b) gamble on FR 2880 (30% the slide blocks you: turn back +40 min), (c) low-clearance car on potholes (20% chance of a scraped oil pan - arrive late). Flagger wait during road work: +20 min.

hazards.name: Mine-tainted water at Tubal Cain
hazards.real_world: Water pouring from the Tubal Cain mine shaft may contain high concentrations of unsavory substances; camps near the mine are littered with debris.
hazards.game_event_idea: Thirsty at the mine stream: (a) walk on to a clean creek (+15 min), (b) filter it anyway (filters don't remove metals; morale penalty and a 'what was that' tummy), (c) drink from your reserve.

hazards.name: Deer Park Road
hazards.season: closed late fall to late spring; dusty in summer
hazards.real_world: Narrow, steep gravel with blind corners, scary drop-offs and few turnouts; not for RVs or trailers.
hazards.game_event_idea: An oncoming truck on a blind corner: (a) back up to a turnout (safe, +5 min), (b) squeeze by (10% chance of a scraped mirror).

hazards.name: Early-season snow on high passes
hazards.real_world: NPS: snow may cover higher reaches in any season; ice axe and self-arrest skills needed when snow-covered; storms move quickly and whiteouts are sudden.
hazards.game_event_idea: Planning in June: the ranger's report says passes are snowy. (a) Bring ice axe + microspikes (+weight), (b) pick a low-elevation trip instead (Dose Forks, Gray Wolf from Slab Camp), (c) go anyway with trail runners (50% turn back at the snow line).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Olympic marmot
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Endemic to the Olympics; WTA notes whistling marmots on Elk Mountain's sunny slopes. NPS says it is now rarely seen at Deer Park, likely due to non-native coyote predation.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Helper character: a marmot whose whistle warns of incoming weather; sketchable for the journal.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Olympic chipmunk
wildlife_and_plants.notes: NPS lists it among Olympic Peninsula endemics. Chipmunks and gray jays raid careless campers at Camp Handy (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Comic thief event if snacks aren't stored.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Canada jay (gray jay)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: WTA: Camp Handy is 'a popular cafeteria for gray jays and chipmunks'.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Friendly but sneaky camp visitor; teach not to feed wildlife.

wildlife_and_plants.name: American black bear
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Slopes below Hayden Pass favored by foraging bears (WTA); canisters required park-wide.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Gentle Bear character who advises on the climb (homage); hazard if food stored badly.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Roosevelt elk
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Present in the park's valleys; specific West Fork sightings not verified in sources used.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Sketchable herd at dusk in a meadow (rare event).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Black-tailed deer
wildlife_and_plants.notes: WTA notes deer frequent the Deer Park area; Deer Park's name.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Morning visitor at camp; sketchable.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Rodents at Royal Lake (mice, chipmunks, squirrels)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: NPS 6/5/26: visitor reports of problematic rodents trying to get into food around Royal Lake.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Night-time hazard event tied to food storage.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Mountain goat (non-native, removed)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Introduced to the Olympics; 325 translocated to the Cascades 2018-2020 and lethal removal through 2022; park now in a maintenance phase with very few left.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Ranger story/lore only; a rare 'did I just see a goat?' moment that a ranger asks you to report.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Coyote
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Non-native coyote predation is likely why marmots are now rare at Deer Park (NPS brochure).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Distant howl at Deer Park campground; lore about marmots.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Flett's violet (Viola flettii)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Endemic violet of rocky outcrops and talus in the northeastern and eastern Olympics; blooms June-August; rare (about 36 known populations).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Journal-sketch rarity: only sketch, never pick (mirrors the book's ending).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Piper's bellflower (Olympic bellflower, Campanula piperi)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Olympic endemic of rock crevices on drier subalpine and alpine slopes; NPS notes it blooming on Blue Mountain's summit near Deer Park.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: A candidate 'golden glow' stand-in for the summit find (blue, not gold) or a page in the field guide.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Glacier lily (yellow avalanche lily, Erythronium grandiflorum)
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Golden-yellow lily that blooms right at the melting snow's edge in subalpine meadows (general botany; site-specific occurrences not verified in sources used).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Best homage 'golden glow': a yellow flower glowing at the edge of the snow at sunset - sketch it, don't pick it.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Pacific rhododendron
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Pink spring-blooming tunnels on Deer Ridge, the Lower Gray Wolf and Tubal Cain trails; a splash of pink on the Main Fork in late spring (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Seasonal scenery change in late May-June.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Subalpine fir
wildlife_and_plants.notes: WTA: on Grand Ridge, firs clone themselves from skirt-like branches pressed down by snow, making 'islands' of trees.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Field-guide tree page; tree islands in EGA art.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Whitebark pine
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Clumps of contorted whitebark pine above Boulder Shelter on the way to Marmot Pass (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Twisted-tree landmark; field-guide page.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Alaska yellow-cedar
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Clumpy Alaska cedar along the upper Main Fork (WTA); an Alaska cedar must be hugged to climb a ledge on the Lake Constance route (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: The 'helpful tree' on the Constance scramble.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Cow parsnip
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Waist-high 'parsnip' meadows above the Gray Wolf junction that soak legs after rain (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Wet-brush hazard; rain pants save morale.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Fireweed
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Bear Camp's shelter stands in a profusion of fireweed (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Magenta EGA accent in the Bear Camp scene.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Huckleberry
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Huckleberries in some Buckhorn Lake camps (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Forage-a-snack event (share with Bear?).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Devil's club
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Part of the Main Fork understory (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Prickly hazard when bushwhacking around blowdown (gloves help).

wildlife_and_plants.name: Pacific yew
wildlife_and_plants.notes: A few yews along the Main Fork (WTA).
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Field-guide tree page.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Lupine, paintbrush, avalanche lily, phlox, stonecrop, chocolate lily, columbine
wildlife_and_plants.notes: Wildflowers named for Grand Ridge (avalanche lily, paintbrush, lupine) and Deer Ridge (stonecrop, phlox, chocolate lily, columbine, buttercup, lupine) by WTA.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Flower spread of the field guide; collect sketches.

wildlife_and_plants.name: Orange crustose lichen on Maiden Peak shale
wildlife_and_plants.notes: WTA: Maiden Peak is mostly shale and slate broken with orange lichen.
wildlife_and_plants.game_idea: Small sketch target with an orange EGA highlight.

permit_and_rules.rule: A wilderness camping permit is required for every overnight trip in Olympic National Park, year-round; permits must be obtained in advance on Recreation.gov, by phone, or at a Wilderness Information Center - no paper trailhead self-registration.

Fees: $8 per adult (16+) per night, youth 15 and under free, plus a $6 non-refundable reservation fee per permit; annual Olympic Wilderness Pass $45 covers nightly fees (not the $6). Cancel 3+ days ahead for a camping-fee refund.

Summer-season permits (May 15 - October 15) are released April 15 at 7:00 AM Pacific; high-elevation areas are typically bookable online only from about mid-July to mid-October; otherwise call the WIC (360-565-3100).

Quota areas in this region: Royal Basin/Royal Lake; Lake Constance; Grand and Badger Valleys (includes everything from Deer Park to Obstruction Point, i.e., Roaring Winds). Quota permits are bulk-released and no extra availability opens later; deviating from your itinerary in a quota area is not allowed except in emergencies.

Nightly caps seen on Recreation.gov (Oct 2026 availability data): Royal Lake 8 parties/30 people; Royal Lake group site 12 people; Royal Creek 3 parties/30 people; Lower Royal Meadow 2 parties/12 people; Upper Royal Basin 3 parties/12 people (WIC only); Lake Constance 6 parties/20 people plus group site; Roaring Winds 1 party/6 people. Non-quota camps show 100.

Park-approved bear canisters (animal-resistant food containers) are required in all Olympic NP wilderness camp areas for all food, garbage and scented items; hanging food (bear wires or self-made hangs) is prohibited. WIC loans canisters first-come, first-served (no reservations).

Royal Basin: camp in designated sites only; no campfires; canisters required (trees unsuitable for hanging, no bear wires); composting toilets at Royal Lake; trail closed to stock at the park boundary; Royal Lake permits are for the lake, not the Upper Basin (Upper Basin by WIC arrangement).

Campfires are prohibited above 3,500 ft throughout Olympic NP and in Buckhorn Wilderness (which also bans gathering wood above 3,500 ft). Where allowed (e.g., Dose Forks, Big Timber, Diamond Meadows, Deception Creek, Three Forks, Gray Wolf, Camp Ellis), use existing rings and dead-and-down wood only.
Lake Constance: designated sites only; no fires; max group 6 (group site 7-12); stock prohibited; composting toilet (don't urinate in it).

Maximum group size 12 in Olympic NP wilderness (6 at many subalpine camps such as Royal Lake, Lower Royal Meadow, Roaring Winds, Lake Constance, Lower Cameron, Camp Ellis, Sunnybrook Meadows, Home Lake); Buckhorn Wilderness max 12 people and 8 head of stock.
Pets and bicycles are not permitted on Olympic NP trails; bikes may be ridden on the closed Dosewallips Road to the old ranger station.
Parking at the Upper Dungeness trailhead requires a Northwest Forest Pass, interagency (America the Beautiful) pass, or $5 day fee (cashless scan-and-pay).
Olympic NP entrance fee/pass applies at Deer Park and Obstruction Point (Hurricane Ridge entrance).

Buckhorn Wilderness (Olympic National Forest) camps - Camp Handy, Boulder Shelter, Camp Mystery, Shelter Rock, Buckhorn Lake, Slide Camp - do not need an Olympic NP permit; wilderness regulations apply (no caching gear over 24 h, weed-free feed, no tethering stock to trees).
Human waste: use toilets where provided; otherwise bury 6-8 in deep at least 200 ft from water, trails and camps and pack out toilet paper.
Deer Park Campground: 14 tent sites, first-come first-served, $15/night, open June to mid-October; no potable water; firewood gathering prohibited.

Hidden 'secret' camp/cross-country zones exist on Recreation.gov but are not bookable online - arrange through the WIC (360-565-3100): Upper Royal Basin, Deception Basin, Royal Basin Cross Country, Cedar Lake, Graywolf River Cross Country, Grand Pass, Burdick Creek, Anderson Glacier Camp, LaCrosse Junction, Thousand Acre Meadow, Lost Pass & Lost Basin (3 Sons), Dee Lake, Wildcat Lake, Dosewallips River Cross Country, Dose Campground, Deer Park Campground (Winter).

Stock: West Fork Dose stock must use designated stock camps at Big Timber and Diamond Meadows; stock prohibited on Lower Gray Wolf, Lake Constance and Royal Basin (in park); Grand Ridge and Cameron Pass trails not recommended for stock.

conditions_2026.note: Dosewallips Road closed to vehicles at the washout outside the park, 6.5 mi below the old campground; open to pedestrians and bicycles.
Main Fork Dosewallips: 19 trees down between the Constance Pass junction and Deception Creek (largest 3.5 ft) and 21 between Deception Creek and Hayden Pass (largest 3 ft); Hayden Pass snow-free.
Hayden Pass Trail (west of the pass, Elwha side): eroded, exposed section; slow, exposed hiking with many blowdowns from the 2016 Hayes Fire.
West Fork Dosewallips snow-free to Anderson Pass; footbridge above Diamond Meadow out - ford the river a couple of times between Diamond and Honeymoon Meadows. Anderson Moraine trail: patchy snow.
Lake Constance Route snow-free to the lake; burn-area blowdown and route-finding; south vault toilet closed, north composting toilet operational.
Constance Pass Trail: no water until ~0.5 mi below Sunnybrook Meadows; tread poor/failing in rock-slide sections above the meadows; not stock accessible through Olympic NF.
Royal Basin Trail snow-free to Royal Lake; problematic rodents at Royal Lake; quota area; no self-pay box at the trailhead anymore; closed to stock.

Upper Gray Wolf: washout on Lower Gray Wolf Trail; Upper Trail and Slab Camp Trail not accessible from the Lower Gray Wolf trailhead (use Slab Camp). Cedar Lake way trail hard to find/follow with many downed trees.
Cameron Creek Trail: two creek crossings can be difficult or impossible in heavy rain or melt; northern foot-log can be partly submerged. Cameron Pass Trail overgrown below Cameron Basin.
Deer Park Road open (gravel, narrow); Obstruction Point Road open; Hurricane Ridge Road open (may close for weather).
conditions_2026.info_date: Deer Park 2026-06-09; Obstruction Pt 2026-06-17; Hurricane Ridge 2026-05-04

conditions_2026.note: Hurricane Ridge 2026 utility rehabilitation: construction in main parking lot, no potable water on Hurricane Ridge, possible rolling closures (affects Obstruction Point drivers).

USFS: NF-2870 resurfacing (first 5 mi from the Lost Mountain Road junction) beginning Oct 7, 2026 - flaggers, single-lane traffic, weekday closures; affects Upper Dungeness, Tubal Cain, Gray Wolf and Ned Hill trailheads.
FR 2880 rockslide about 0.5 mi past Dungeness Forks Campground; Dungeness-area trailheads still reachable via FR 2870 (Taylor Cutoff/Lost Mountain roads). 2026 clearance not confirmed.
Dosewallips Flats Fire (Aug 2025) temporarily closed the Dosewallips Road; by May 2026 trail crews were biking the old road to the campground.
Royal Basin spring 2026: trail mostly dry to Royal Lake by late April/early May with snow patches above 4,600 ft; trail lost in snow/marsh near 5,300 ft; continuous snow to the upper moraine basin.
Bear Gulch Fire (2025) closures are in the North Fork Skokomish/Staircase area, outside this region; no fire closures listed for the northeast in 2026.
Park-approved bear canister list updated; canisters required in all wilderness areas.

uncertain_claims: Royal Glacier: no 'Royal Glacier' appears in USGS GNIS; climbing sources describe a small (stagnant) glacier remnant on Mount Deception's northwest side above Royal Basin (sometimes called the Deception Glacier). Node 'royal_glacier' uses an informal name; location, elevation and distance are null.

Main Fork Dosewallips mileage: NPS trail-conditions page lists Dose Forks to Hayden Pass as 11.3 mi; WTA gives 15.0 mi from the old trailhead (13.6 from Dose Forks), Hiking Project 13.1 mi. The NPS GIS trail line (~14.3 mi raw, typically 5% short) supports WTA, which is used.

Dosewallips road walk: NPS and some Recreation.gov text say 6.5 mi to the old campground; other Recreation.gov text says 5 mi; Frommers 5.5 mi; WTA '5+ mi' to Lake Constance. Parking location: NPS GPX labels the washout at 47.7388,-123.0736, but OSM drivable road ends ~1.1-1.3 mi east (47.7416,-123.0495), which is used as the trailhead; segment split (1.3 + 3.7 + 1.5) is approximate.
Lake Constance elevation: NPS conditions 4,700 ft, NPS route page and WTA 4,800 ft, USGS DEM ~4,720-4,760 ft. Route length 1.8 (NPS route), 2.0 (NPS conditions), 2.2 mi (WTA).
Lost Pass elevation: GNIS/Wikipedia/DEM 5,571 ft; NPS trail-conditions ranges imply 6,200 ft; some trip reports say ~6,500 ft (likely confusion with nearby Lost Peak, 6,515 ft).
Grand Pass elevation: not found in an authoritative source; 6,420 ft is from the USGS DEM along the trail line (GNIS point reads 6,348 ft). Owned by the Grand Valley region.
Constance Pass Trail high point: DEM along the NPS trail line suggests the trail crests ~6,500 ft between Sunnybrook Meadows and Constance Pass; NPS lists the trail's top as 5,850 ft.

Constance Pass Trail splits (3.4 / 1.7 / 0.4 mi) are the NPS GIS line scaled to NPS's 7.8 mi total; Recreation.gov's camp blurbs imply different values (e.g., Sunnybrook 11.7 mi from the Dose road end).
Home Lake to Boulder Shelter: WTA says 3.6 mi but also 1.0 + 2.9 = 3.9 mi; 3.6 used (matches Recreation.gov's 10 mi from the Upper Dungeness TH).

West Fork splits (2.7, 2.6, 2.2, 0.5, 0.1, 1.0 mi) blend Recreation.gov's road-end mileages with NPS's 9.0-9.1 mi total; a 2025 trip report found mileages longer (Anderson Pass ~18.25 mi from the road end).

Royal Basin splits: Royal Creek camp ~4.0 mi, Lower Royal Meadow ~6.3 mi from the trailhead are NPS GIS distances scaled to NPS's 7.2 mi; Upper Royal Basin 0.75 (WTA), 1.05 (OSM) or 1.5 mi (Hiking Project) past the lake - 1.0 used.

Royal Lake site count: about 9 individual sites + 1 group site counted from the NPS camp map image; Recreation.gov caps at 8 parties/night (Oct 2026 data). Summer quotas might differ from October values.

Royal Creek camp campfires: Recreation.gov says campfires permitted in established rings, but the camp sits near 3,670 ft (above the park's 3,500-ft fire line). Same conflict at Falls Camp and Lower Cameron.
Slide Camp: location and elevation (2,200 ft) estimated from Mountaineers/WTA trip descriptions; lat/lon unknown.

Slab Camp to park boundary: USFS pages disagree (Upper Gray Wolf enters park after 2.7 mi vs. 'follows it 5.8 miles to the boundary'); Mountaineers says boundary ~6 mi from trailhead; OSM 5.8 mi total used.
Burdick Creek camp coordinates/elevation estimated by placing WTA's 5.5-mi mark on the NPS trail line.
Half Acre Rock elevation (~3,000 ft) and position estimated from WTA's 0.8-mi mark on the NPS route line.

Gain/loss values are mostly computed from the USGS 1/3 arc-second DEM sampled every ~90 m along NPS GIS or OpenStreetMap trail lines (3-point smoothing), and can differ from guidebook figures by 10-20%.
Shelter Rock Camp elevation: DEM at OSM point ~3,820 ft vs WTA 3,600 ft and SummitPost 3,650 ft.
Camp Handy distance: 3.2 mi (USFS) vs 3.4 mi (WTA); Marmot Pass from Big Quilcene TH: 5.3 mi (USFS) vs ~5.75 mi (WTA).

Dosewallips Campground permit status: Recreation.gov has a hidden 'Dose Campground' division (implying a permit), while a 2024 trip-report comment says no permit is needed there; also Elkhorn Campground (USFS) on the road was said not to need a permit.
